rules.description: Package name closely resembles a trusted package but is not published by its verified publisher.
rules.detection_condition: similarity.best_match() returns relation confusable, edit, extra_words or missing_words, and the package owner is not a verified publisher of the matched trusted package. Severity by evidence strength: confusable HIGH, edit MEDIUM, extra_words/missing_words LOW.
rules.explanation: Typosquatting publishes a package whose name differs from a popular one by a character, a separator or an extra word. A similar name alone does not prove intent: many legitimate packages have similar names.
rules.recommendation: Compare the name character by character with the trusted package. If you meant the trusted package, declare it as owner/name with an exact version.
limitations: Only packages in databases/trusted_packages.json are protected.
Short names (under 5 characters) are not compared by edit distance.
Legitimate packages with similar names by other publishers will also match.

Calibration on 1,152 real registry names near the trusted names: 23 packages from non-verified publishers matched a non-exact relation (6 edit, 17 extra_words, 0 missing_words); most are legitimate extension libraries. See docs/similarity_calibration.json.

rules.description: Package has the same name as a trusted package but a different publisher.
rules.detection_condition: Normalised package name equals a trusted package name or alias, and the owner is not the verified registry owner or an additional verified publisher.
rules.explanation: Forks and re-uploads under another account receive code from someone other than the verified upstream maintainer. Many forks are benign, but the code is not the code that was reviewed upstream.
rules.recommendation: Use the verified publisher (owner/name) unless you deliberately depend on this fork and have reviewed it.
limitations: Maintainer changes or organisation moves that are not yet in trusted_packages.json will be reported.

rules.description: Dependency does not exist in the PlatformIO Registry.
rules.detection_condition: GET /v3/packages/<owner>/library/<name> returns 404, or a search finds no library with exactly this name.
rules.explanation: The build will fail today, and if someone later publishes a package with this name, PlatformIO would install that package. Names produced by mistakes or by AI code assistants are a known source of this problem.
rules.recommendation: Check the spelling and owner. Replace the entry with the package you actually need.
limitations: Private registries and packages removed after the cache was filled are not distinguished.

rules.description: Dependency is declared without an owner and several registry publishers use this name.
rules.detection_condition: The entry has no owner and the registry search returns libraries with exactly this name from more than one owner (LOW when only one owner publishes it).
rules.explanation: Without owner/ the publisher is chosen at install time. The project does not state whose code it expects.
limitations: ShipSafe does not reproduce PlatformIO's exact resolution order; it lists every exact-name publisher.

rules.description: Pinned version is not published in the registry.
applies_to: lib_deps registry entry with an exact version
rules.detection_condition: The version is an exact number and is not in the package's 'versions' list returned by the registry.
rules.explanation: A version that was never published cannot be installed as written; it often indicates a mistyped or invented version.
rules.recommendation: Use a version listed by the registry.

rules.description: Source repository differs from the trusted package's upstream repository.
rules.detection_condition: The package name matches a trusted package, but the registry repository_url, or the git URL in lib_deps, does not point at the verified upstream repository.
rules.explanation: The code comes from a different repository than the one the trusted entry was verified against.
rules.recommendation: Confirm that the repository is the intended upstream, or switch to the verified package.
limitations: Repository URLs are self-declared by publishers and may be stale after a project moves.

rules.detection_condition: The registry response has no repository_url, or no description.
rules.explanation: Without a repository link the published code cannot be traced to a public source history.
rules.recommendation: Prefer packages that link to a public source repository, or review the package archive manually.
limitations: Missing metadata is common for small legitimate packages.

rules.description: Registry metadata could not be retrieved; identity checks are incomplete.
rules.detection_condition: The registry was unreachable, timed out, rate-limited the client or returned an invalid response, and no cached answer exists.
rules.explanation: Unknown is not the same as safe. Name similarity against the trusted database still ran because it needs no network access.
rules.recommendation: Re-run the scan when the registry is reachable.

rules.description: Dependency is fetched from a URL instead of the registry.
rules.detection_condition: lib_deps, platform or platform_packages contains a git or archive URL. INFO when pinned to a commit or tag, LOW otherwise.
rules.explanation: URL dependencies carry no registry metadata. Without a commit or tag, every build may download different code.
rules.recommendation: Pin the URL to a commit hash or tag (#ref), or use the registry package.
limitations: ShipSafe cannot tell a tag from a branch name; only commit hashes are fully immutable.

rules.description: Installed package does not match the declared dependency.
rules.detection_condition: The installed package's owner differs from the declared owner, or its registry ID differs from the trusted package's registry ID.
rules.explanation: The code that was actually built is not the package that platformio.ini asks for.
rules.recommendation: Delete .pio/libdeps and reinstall, then compare the result.
limitations: Only checked when the upload contains .pio/libdeps.

rules.description: Local dependency: no registry metadata; its source code is analysed by the security engine.
applies_to: file://, symlink:// or relative path dependency
rules.detection_condition: lib_deps entry refers to a local folder.
rules.explanation: Local code is not covered by registry identity checks.
rules.recommendation: Make sure the local folder is part of your reviewed source tree.
limitations: Folders outside the uploaded archive cannot be analysed.
